name: Sponsor of Your Problems
description: For two integers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, we define $$$f(a, b)$$$ as the number of positions in the decimal representation of the numbers $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ where their digits are the same. For example, $$$f(12, 21) = 0$$$, $$$f(31, 37) = 1$$$, $$$f(19891, 18981) = 2$$$, $$$f(54321, 24361) = 3$$$. You are given two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ of the same length in decimal representation. Consider all integers $$$l \leq x \leq r$$$. Your task is to find the minimum value of $$$f(l, x) + f(x, r)$$$.
input_specification: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. Each test case consists of a single line containing two integers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ ($$$1 \leq l \leq r \lt 10^9$$$). It is guaranteed that the numbers $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ have the same length in decimal representation and do not have leading zeros.
output_specification: For each test case, output the minimum value of $$$f(l, x) + f(x, r)$$$ among all integer values $$$l \leq x \leq r$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2121E — Sponsor of Your Problems [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
